raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

For complete tool schemas, the non-strict GLM47 grammar allows known argument keys to repeat without a bound. If the model emits an unknown key, it can keep generating repeated known keys until the output limit.

## Modifications

Limit argument pairs in each call to the number of keys in a complete schema. Keys remain optional and can appear in any order; duplicates are still allowed within the limit. Incomplete or free-form schemas retain the existing rule. The parser keeps the last value for a repeated key.

## Accuracy Tests

Focused grammar regressions and scoped formatting pass on the updated branch, including bounded, open and empty schemas. Earlier direct XGrammar and llguidance checks accepted optional and reordered keys and rejected excess pairs. The limit applies within one call, so the model can still start another call. The looping requests have not been replayed with a live model.

Run the unit suites with `python -m pytest` and formatting with `pre-commit run --files <changed-files>`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

CPU measurements with the GLM-4.7-Flash tokenizer showed similar grammar compilation and per-token mask times across both runs. The interquartile ranges overlap, and the measurements cover grammar work only.


## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+    def test_argument_pairs_are_bounded_by_schema_keys(self):
+        # A repeated key must not let one call grow until max_tokens.
+        for keys in (["query"], ["query", "from", "to"]):
+            ebnf = self._ebnf({"properties": {k: {"type": "string"} for k in keys}})
+            grammar = self.compiler.compile_grammar(xgr.Grammar.from_ebnf(ebnf))
+            pairs = [f"<arg_key>{k}</arg_key><arg_value>v</arg_value>" for k in keys]
+            cases = {
+                "".join(pairs): True,
+                "".join(reversed(pairs)): True,
+                "": True,
+                "".join(pairs) + pairs[0]: False,
+                pairs[0] * (len(keys) + 1): False,
+            }
+            for backend, accepts in (
+                ("xgrammar", lambda text: self._accepts(grammar, text)),
+                ("llguidance", lambda text: self._llguidance_accepts(ebnf, text)),
+            ):
+                for arguments, expected in cases.items():
+                    text = f"<tool_call>alpha{arguments}</tool_call>"
+                    with self.subTest(backend=backend, text=text):
+                        self.assertEqual(accepts(text), expected)
+
+    def test_complete_zero_key_schemas_reject_argument_pairs(self):
+        """Closed no-argument tools reject pairs; open schemas still accept them."""
+        closed = {"properties": {}, "additionalProperties": False}
+        schemas = [
+            (closed, False),
+            ({"additionalProperties": False}, False),
+            ({"allOf": [closed]}, False),
+            ({}, True),
+            ({"properties": {}}, True),
+            ({"properties": {}, "additionalProperties": True}, True),
+            ({"$ref": "#/$defs/args", "$defs": {"args": closed}}, True),
+            ({"properties": {}, "allOf": [closed]}, True),
+        ]
+        pair = "<arg_key>unknown</arg_key><arg_value>v</arg_value>"
+        for schema, allows_pairs in schemas:
+            ebnf = self._ebnf(schema)
+            grammar = self.compiler.compile_grammar(xgr.Grammar.from_ebnf(ebnf))
+            for backend, accepts in (
+                ("xgrammar", lambda text: self._accepts(grammar, text)),
+                ("llguidance", lambda text: self._llguidance_accepts(ebnf, text)),
+            ):
+                for arguments in ("", pair, pair * 3):
+                    text = f"<tool_call>alpha{arguments}</tool_call>"
+                    with self.subTest(backend=backend, schema=schema, text=text):
+                        self.assertEqual(accepts(text), not arguments or allows_pairs)
